children: A federal change could give manufactured housing a new shot at the entry-level market by lowering production costs and making factory-built homes look more like site-built homes, Realtor.com says. But local zoning rules will determine whether that opportunity becomes new housing. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act removes a longstanding requirement that manufactured homes be built on a permanent steel chassis for towing. The change can reduce material costs, enable more flexible installation, and eliminate the step-up appearance associated with mobile homes. Only about 17% of zoned land nationwide expressly allows mobile and/or manufactured housing parks. Municipalities can restrict manufactured housing by excluding it from regular residential zones, limiting it to commercial, industrial or agricultural areas. (chris.wack@wsj.com)
